newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp bid for Loewen met warily.
newsitem.headline: Service Corp bid for Loewen met warily.

text.p: Wall Street takeover traders, hurt recently by a slew of unsolicited bids that have failed to materialize, reacted warily to Service Corp International's offer for Loewen Group Inc.
Although shares of Loewen traded in the U.S. soared from Monday's levels, the stock remained sharply below Service Corp's bid of $43 per share. By late morning, the stock was up six at 39-3/4.
Traders cited uncertainty about whether Service Corp would be willing to pursue a hostile takeover if the $43 per share offer were rebuffed by Loewen.
"This is a bear hug. It's not a tender offer. Guys are really trying to protect themselves these days, having been left standing at the altar with so many of these bear hugs," one trader said.
Traders also cited potential antitrust issues that could emerge from a union between the two huge funeral home operators.
In disclosing the offer, Service Corp said it had tried to reach Loewen several times since September 11, but calls had not been returned.
Loewen did not have any immediate comment on the bid.
"This is quite surprising. I think they're very serious about it," said Todd Berko, analyst at PaineWebber.
The bid by Service Corp comes as both companies have been buying North America's privately-owned funeral homes.
In June, Loewen teamed up with investment bank Blackstone Group to buy Prime Succession Inc, the largest privately-held funeral home operator in the U.S., for $295 million.
